lesson_scope: Proving that a line and a curve always meet (or always have 2 distinct intersections) for all real values of a parameter (m, k, c) by showing the discriminant D satisfies D >= 0 (or D > 0), typically via a sum of squares / completed-square form.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: proving distinct intersections for all real m using sum of squares discriminant.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of proving D > 0 using m^2 >= 0.

hints: Since $m^2 \ge 0$ for all real $m$, $D = m^2 + 16 \ge 16 > 0$, so there are always two distinct real intersection points.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations to form the quadratic intersection equation:
$$x^2 - 4 = mx$$
$$x^2 - mx - 4 = 0$$

Evaluate the discriminant $D = b^2 - 4ac$:
$$D = (-m)^2 - 4(1)(-4) = m^2 + 16$$

Conclude that $D > 0$ for all real $m$:
$$\text{Since } m^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } m \in \mathbb{R}, \quad D = m^2 + 16 \ge 16 > 0.$$
$$\text{Hence, the line meets the curve at two distinct points for all real } m.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates to $x^2 - mx - 4 = 0$ and computes $D = (-m)^2 - 4(1)(-4) = m^2 + 16$.
States $m^2 \ge 0 \implies D \ge 16 > 0$ for all real $m$, concluding 2 distinct intersection points.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: completing the square on the discriminant to prove D > 0.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of completing square on discriminant.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations and set to zero:
$$x^2 - kx + 2k = 2x + 1$$
$$x^2 - (k + 2)x + (2k - 1) = 0$$

Find and complete the square on the discriminant $D$:
$$D = (k + 2)^2 - 4(1)(2k - 1)$$
$$D = k^2 + 4k + 4 - 8k + 4 = k^2 - 4k + 8$$
$$D = (k - 2)^2 + 4$$

Explain why the line and curve always meet:
$$\text{Since } (k - 2)^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } k \in \mathbb{R}, \quad D \ge 4 > 0.$$
$$\text{Therefore, the equation always has two distinct real solutions for all real } k.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that $(k - 2)^2 \ge 0 \implies D \ge 4 > 0$, so real intersections always exist.

hints: The square term $(k + 5)^2 \ge 0$ for all real $k$.

State the value of $k$ where the minimum occurs:

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: establishing completed-square discriminant on non-monic curve and minimizing root separation.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the curve and line equations:
$$2x^2 + 3x + 1 = mx + 4$$
$$2x^2 + (3 - m)x - 3 = 0$$

Calculate the discriminant:
$$D = (3 - m)^2 - 4(2)(-3) = (m - 3)^2 + 24$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires deducing distinct roots for all m and finding minimizing value.

hints: Since $(m - 3)^2 \ge 0$, $D \ge 24 > 0$ for all real $m$, so the line and curve always meet at two distinct points.
The distance between intersection $x$-coordinates is $|x_2 - x_1| = \dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{a} = \dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2}$.
This distance is minimized when $D$ is minimized, which occurs when $(m - 3)^2 = 0 \implies m = 3$.

walkthrough.text:
Deduce distinct intersections for all real $m$:
$$\text{For all } m \in \mathbb{R}, \quad (m - 3)^2 \ge 0 \implies D = (m - 3)^2 + 24 \ge 24 > 0$$
$$\text{Thus, } D > 0 \text{ for all real } m, \text{ so the line and curve meet at two distinct points.}$$

Find the value of $m$ minimizing the separation:
$$\text{Separation } |x_2 - x_1| = \dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{(m - 3)^2 + 24}}{2}$$
$$\text{This is minimized when } (m - 3)^2 = 0 \implies m = 3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Deduces that $(m - 3)^2 \ge 0 \implies D \ge 24 > 0$, so 2 distinct points exist for all $m$.
Identifies that separation $|x_2 - x_1| = \dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2}$ is minimized when $D$ is minimized at $m = 3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: simplifying parametric discriminant and evaluating domain boundaries for distinct intersections and tangency.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires simplifying algebraic discriminant in terms of p.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the discriminant with $a = p - 2, b = 2p, c = p + 3$:
$$D = (2p)^2 - 4(p - 2)(p + 3)$$

Expand and simplify:
$$D = 4p^2 - 4(p^2 + p - 6) = 4p^2 - 4p^2 - 4p + 24 = 24 - 4p$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding parameter range for distinct roots and tangency value.

hints: For two distinct points on the $x$-axis, set $D > 0 \implies 24 - 4p > 0 \implies 4p < 24 \implies p < 6$.
Remember the given constraint $p > 2$, so the interval is $2 < p < 6$.
For tangency to the $x$-axis, set $D = 0 \implies 24 - 4p = 0 \implies p = 6$.

walkthrough.text:
For two distinct real roots, require $D > 0$:
$$24 - 4p > 0 \implies 4p < 24 \implies p < 6$$
$$\text{Combining with the given condition } p > 2 \text{ gives } 2 < p < 6.$$

For tangency to the $x$-axis, require $D = 0$:
$$24 - 4p = 0 \implies p = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $24 - 4p > 0$ and combines with $p > 2$ to get $2 < p < 6$.

hints: Line $L$ through $(0, 2)$ with gradient $m$ has equation $y = mx + 2$.
Equate line and curve: $x^2 - 3x + 1 = mx + 2 \implies x^2 - (m + 3)x - 1 = 0$.
Since $(m + 3)^2 \ge 0$ for all $m \in \mathbb{R}$, $D \ge 4 > 0$, so two distinct intersection points exist for all $m$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the equation of the line $L$ passing through $(0, 2)$:
$$y = mx + 2$$

Equate the line and curve equations:
$$x^2 - 3x + 1 = mx + 2$$
$$x^2 - (m + 3)x - 1 = 0$$

Calculate the discriminant and prove strict positivity:
$$D = (m + 3)^2 - 4(1)(-1) = (m + 3)^2 + 4$$
$$\text{For all } m \in \mathbb{R}, \quad (m + 3)^2 \ge 0 \implies D = (m + 3)^2 + 4 \ge 4 > 0$$
$$\text{Hence, } L \text{ meets the parabola at two distinct points for every real value of } m.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that $(m + 3)^2 \ge 0 \implies D \ge 4 > 0$, so two distinct intersection points exist for all $m$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding parametric coordinates of midpoint of chord.

hints: From the quadratic $x^2 - (m + 3)x - 1 = 0$, the sum of roots is $x_1 + x_2 = m + 3$.
Substitute $x_M$ into the line equation $y = mx + 2$: $y_M = m\left(\dfrac{m + 3}{2}\right) + 2 = \dfrac{m^2 + 3m + 4}{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the $x$-coordinate of the midpoint using the sum of roots formula:
$$x_1 + x_2 = -\dfrac{b}{a} = m + 3$$
$$x_M = \dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2} = \dfrac{m + 3}{2}$$

Find the $y$-coordinate using the line equation $y = mx + 2$:
$$y_M = m x_M + 2 = m\left(\dfrac{m + 3}{2}\right) + 2$$
$$y_M = \dfrac{m^2 + 3m}{2} + \dfrac{4}{2} = \dfrac{m^2 + 3m + 4}{2}$$
$$\text{Midpoint coordinates: } \left(\dfrac{m + 3}{2}, \dfrac{m^2 + 3m + 4}{2}\right)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses sum of roots $x_1 + x_2 = m + 3$ to find midpoint $x_M = \dfrac{m + 3}{2}$.
Substitutes into line equation to show $y_M = m\left(\dfrac{m + 3}{2}\right) + 2 = \dfrac{m^2 + 3m + 4}{2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: two-curve intersection discriminant proof D = -4(k + 2)^2 <= 0, proving curves never cross at 2 points and finding unique tangency.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires establishing intersection equation between two parabolas and finding discriminant.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the equations of the two parabolas:
$$x^2 + 2kx + 3 = -x^2 + 4x - (k^2 + 1)$$
$$2x^2 + (2k - 4)x + (k^2 + 4) = 0$$
$$2x^2 + 2(k - 2)x + (k^2 + 4) = 0$$

Factor out $-4$ to write as a negative perfect square:
$$D = -4(k^2 + 4k + 4) = -4(k + 2)^2$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires proving curves never cross at 2 points and finding unique tangency point.

hints: Since $D$ can never be strictly positive ($D > 0$), the curves never intersect at two distinct points.
The only way they touch is when $D = 0 \implies -4(k + 2)^2 = 0 \implies k = -2$.
When $k = -2$, the intersection equation is $2x^2 - 8x + 8 = 2(x - 2)^2 = 0 \implies x = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Prove that $C_1$ and $C_2$ never cross at two distinct points:
$$\text{For all } k \in \mathbb{R}, \quad (k + 2)^2 \ge 0 \implies D = -4(k + 2)^2 \le 0$$
$$\text{Since } D > 0 \text{ is impossible for any real } k, \text{ the two curves never cross at two distinct points.}$$

Find the only value of $k$ for which the curves touch:
$$D = 0 \implies -4(k + 2)^2 = 0 \implies k = -2$$

Find the coordinates of the common point when $k = -2$:
$$2x^2 + 2(-2 - 2)x + ((-2)^2 + 4) = 0$$
$$2x^2 - 8x + 8 = 0 \implies 2(x - 2)^2 = 0 \implies x = 2$$
$$y = 2^2 + 2(-2)(2) + 3 = 4 - 8 + 3 = -1$$
$$\text{Common point: } (2, -1)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that $(k + 2)^2 \ge 0 \implies D = -4(k + 2)^2 \le 0$ for all real $k$, so $D > 0$ is impossible.
Solves for contact point $x = 2, y = -1$ to give $(2, -1)$.
